Auricular defects, oral clefts and ocular abnormalities define the syndrome; skeletal defects including kyphosis and pectus occur in 30-79%.
CNS leukodystrophy defines SPG2; optic atrophy occurs in 30-79%. Spastic bladder and bowel incontinence reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Intellectual disability and choanal atresia define disease; anal atresia and polydactyly each occur in 30-79%. Eye/GU findings are nonspecific; cardiac defects are occasional.
Clonal eosinophilic leukemia is a blood and marrow neoplasm; destructive involvement of other organs is variable and not established in at least 30%.
Inherited coronary artery disease causes atherosclerosis and myocardial infarction; accompanying hypercholesterolemia is a separate lipid disorder.
Recurrent respiratory infections define disease; bronchiectasis affects 4/13. AGR2-related intestinal dysfunction causes chronic diarrhea in 5/13 (~38%); hepatomegaly alone is insufficient.
Acute diarrheal disease is defined by intestinal dysfunction; an infectious cause is not universal.
Lipoma occupies the conus region of the spinal canal and involves the spinal cord interface.
Benign polyp arises exclusively in the vagina, a reproductive organ outside the defined axes.
Acne affects cutaneous pilosebaceous units; local inflammation alone does not establish an immune-mediated systemic disease.
Preaxial polydactyly, ocular colobomata and intellectual disability are defining manifestations.
Inherited bile acid synthesis defect causes severe cholestatic liver disease. Malabsorption and prolonged coagulation time are downstream effects, not direct bowel or blood disease.
Neurodegeneration causes parkinsonism, dystonia and cognitive decline; dysphagia and abnormal eye movements reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Juvenile cataract defines disease; arrhythmia occurs in 14/19 (~74%), supporting cardiac involvement despite the historical nonsyndromic description.
Cleft hard palate is an oral structural defect. Obstructive sleep apnea is a separately diagnosed complication; hearing impairment occurs in only 5-29%.
Fungal skin/nail infection and sinusitis/pneumonia each occur in 30-79%. Neutropenia and immunodeficiency predispose to infection; supplied keratitis frequency is below threshold.
Recurrent episcleral inflammation is an ocular disorder; a specific autoimmune mechanism is not established by this concept.
Drug-induced hearing loss directly affects auditory function; otologic damage defines this disease.
Congestive liver injury and fibrosis define Fontan-associated liver disease; underlying congenital heart disease and Fontan circulation are antecedent conditions.
Infantile hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is defined by myocardial disease; no additional organ involvement is established.
Dilated cardiomyopathy directly affects myocardium; hepatic or obstetric conditions associated with particular subtypes do not apply across the umbrella.
Inherited sensory-neuron channel dysfunction causes episodic neuropathic pain; upper-body pain does not establish muscle or joint damage.
